purpose: This medication is used to treat acne on the face, chest, or back. It helps clear up existing pimples and prevents new ones from forming. It works best when used consistently as part of your daily skincare routine.
how_it_works: This gel contains two ingredients that fight acne in different ways. Adapalene is a vitamin A-like ingredient that helps unclog pores and keeps skin cells from clumping together, which stops pimples from forming. Benzoyl peroxide kills the bacteria on your skin that cause acne and helps reduce redness and inflammation.
common_side_effects: It is very common to have some dryness, redness, peeling, or mild burning or stinging when you first start using it. Your skin may also feel a bit irritated or itchy at first. These effects usually get better after the first few weeks as your skin gets used to the medication.
warnings: Avoid getting this gel in your eyes, mouth, or nose — it can cause irritation. This product can bleach fabrics, hair, and towels, so be careful with colored linens. Always use sunscreen during the day because this medication makes your skin more sensitive to the sun. Do not use this if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first. Stop using it and call your doctor if you develop severe redness, swelling, or a rash.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of gel to the affected area once a day, usually in the evening after washing your face. Use a gentle, non-irritating cleanser and wait for your skin to dry completely before applying. A little goes a long way — you only need a small pea-sized amount for the face.
